recipes.name: Roasted Asparagus and Mushrooms
ingredients_raw: kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C). Lightly grease a baking tray with nonstick spray.
Place asparagus and mushrooms in a bowl. Drizzle with olive oil, then season with rosemary, salt, and pepper; toss well. Lay vegetables on the prepared tray in an even layer.
Roast in the preheated oven until asparagus is tender, about 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Roasted Asparagus and Mushrooms
raw_recipe.description: These roasted asparagus and mushrooms are flavored with olive oil and rosemary, then cooked at high heat until tender for an easy, tasty side dish.

review.reviewBody: I guess I'm one of the few who prepared this as written--with the rosemary. I used a little less than called for, but it complemented the asparagus and mushrooms well and was a nice addition. Simple, easy, delicious, and makes for a beautiul presentation on the dinner plate.

I roast asparagus all the time and it’s one of our favorites. So I knew immediately that I would lower the oven temperature on this to 400 and cut back on the roasting time significantly - to 8 minutes. The asparagus turned out fine, bright green and crisp tender, as I expected it would, but the mushrooms looked a little dry in spots. I think I’d skip roasting the mushrooms next time and just sauté them separately in a pan, then top the asparagus with them when plating.

I love roasted asparagus but 15 minutes at 450 is way too long; it cooks in about 10 to 11 minutes and is tender but not mushy. It's great with these seasonings as written but also good tossed with shredded or shaved parmesan cheese when it comes out of the oven.

Great recipe. Did not use the rosemary as I did not have any. I used garlic instead. Put the asparagus, mushrooms, garlic, oil, etc in a gallon size bag to mix up the ingredients and then poured out on my foil lined pan. Baked at 400 for about 15-20 minutes and they were perfect. Loved the flavor of the mushrooms and loved the easy recipe. A keeper! Easy recipe - easy clean up.

LOVED this! I used smoked sea salt instead of regular salt. I used a Balsamic/honey thyme vinaigrette instead of just olive oil. Very light & tasty! I simply put all the veggies in a produce bag, tossed with the vinaigrette. Placed the veggies on a parchment lined baking sheet, sprinkled over the rosemary, smoked sea salt & pepper. Roasted for the time suggested! Thanks for a simple & tasty recipe!

This dish turned out really good. Cooking time was not long enough. It took 25 minutes to get the asparagus to my liking. I used thin asparagus. I used dried rosemary and it was great. At the end I added about at tablespoon of balsamic vinegar and sprinkled lemon pepper only because I love it. My husband loved the dish and it was really good to me as well. I gave only 4 stars because the cooking time was off a lot . Flavor was excellent.

Great way to cook asparagus. I used baby portabellas (halved) and fairly thin asparagus spears. I reduced the heat to 400 and baked for 10 minutes (due to the skinnier spears) and it came out perfect. Definitely worth repeating.

Thank you for this great base recipe. I chose to add some white wine, homemade chicken stock and a splash of worcestershire to my olive oil and marinated the veggies for half a day before roasting. Very good. Added fresh thyme sprigs and a little lemon zest to the rosemary, and garlic, green beans and thick red onion slices to the veggies b/c I was very hungry. paired with flash fried lemony rockfish, delicious.

I add pieces (tenders or chunks) of cooked chicken to this and it becomes a one dish meal (mix everything together right on the pan). Fantastic & healthy & EASY. (5 stars even without additions) 
I use 'baby bella' mushrooms. I also will just set the sprigs of rosemary in the pan- you get some of the favor without the tough pieces of rosemary that turn some people off (like my kids...) I've cooked asparagus like this for years and love the addition of mushrooms & rosemary.
Cut the rosemary in half. I love it, but it overwhelms the rest of the flavor and ingredients. Cook 12-14 for thinner stalks of asparagus.
I followed the recipe and it was delicious!
Thanks for the recipe. I followed the recipe but seasoned it with pink Himalayan salt. Tasted nice alongside homemade lasagne.
I did not have fresh rosemary, but used dried and it worked out well. The rosemary enhances both vegetables.
Super easy and delicious. Didn't have any rosemary as it turned out, so just went with kosher salt and pepper. It was awesome. The mushrooms were surprisingly flavorful! Best way to do asparagus!

I followed the recipe exactly, it was very easy. I live in Florida and fresh produce is abundant. I had picked up asparagus and Baby Bella mushrooms yesterday. And I have rosemary growing in my small herb garden. So putting this together took very little effort. Roasting the vegetables helps retain their flavor and the beautiful green color of the asparagus. So pretty and so delicious.
Instead of rosemary I added minced garlic & ginger & some toasted sesame oil along with the olive oil. 15 minutes in a 450 degree oven left the asparagus a little overdone.
